_about: What's new in each version of Manifexus, newest first. Shown in Updates. Write for people, not developers: short, plain sentences about what they can now do. The newest entry's version is what gets built and tagged; older entries can give the "commit" they were released from.

releases.headline: Backups that are much faster and take far less space.
new: A new backup store: the backup before every move, delete and restore now keeps only what changed since the last one. Backing up the same app again usually adds just a few kilobytes, and your backups take a fraction of the space.
Moves back up your app while it's still running, then save the last few changes after it stops, so it's back up sooner, even with lots of data.

Your older backups move into the new store on their own, in the background. Each one is checked file by file before its old copy is removed, and the top of the dashboard shows how it's going and how much space it freed.
improved: Backups are about ten times faster: they now use every core of your server's processor.
Moves start and finish sooner: Manifexus does its checks all at once instead of one at a time.
Browsing, downloading and restoring files from a backup works the same for new and older backups.
fixed: Moving an app back into a stack that had no apps running could leave the app's own folder out of the backup. It's always included now.
The shimmer on “in progress” labels no longer hides part of the words.
Restoring a backup to another folder right after Manifexus started could wrongly say the folder already had files in it.

releases.headline: Faster, and even safer with your stacks.
new: Smarter updates: an update now downloads only what changed, usually just Manifexus's own code (a few MB), instead of the whole app again. Updates shows the real download size before you start. (The first update to this version still downloads more, once.)
Edits you make in the compose file editor are now saved in Restore, so you can put the file back the way it was.
improved: The dashboard refreshes about three times faster, asks your server for less, and pauses while its tab is in the background.
Manifexus opens faster: screens you rarely use, like the file editor, load only when you first open them.
Typing in search stays smooth, even with lots of stacks.
An update never restarts Manifexus in the middle of a move, restore or delete; it waits for it to finish first.
Choosing a shorter time in Keep Backups For now tells you how many backups would be removed, and asks before removing them.
If Manifexus can't measure an app's data before deleting it, the backup stays on, so nothing is lost by mistake.
When something doesn't go through (saving a custom name, pinning or deleting a backup), Manifexus now says so instead of looking like it worked.
If Manifexus itself isn't answering (for example while it restarts), the message says so, instead of blaming Docker.
fixed: Stacks whose file is called compose.yaml can now be moved into, restored and deleted properly. Before, a second file could be written beside it and the move would fail.
Your settings and your Restore history can no longer be lost if Manifexus is stopped while saving them.
Two restores, or a restore and a move, can no longer change the same stack at the same time.
Closing Restore or Move during a restore or move and opening it again shows its progress again.
The Move screen keeps showing the names of the apps being moved until it's done.
A backup or move no longer waits for hours if its helper is removed partway through.
Updates no longer get stuck on "Updating" with no way to close the screen, and the nightly automatic update works again after a failed one.
App Details shows a new name or icon right away, and never shows another app's check results.
The file editor keeps working after Reconnect, and only Manifexus's own page can open it.
Cancelling a backup download now stops it on the server too.
Updating Manifexus shows one download size that stays the same, counting only what really needs downloading, instead of a size that kept changing.

releases.headline: Your stacks now fit together like puzzle pieces.
new: Stacks fit together like puzzle pieces: a big stack no longer leaves empty space beside or inside it, because smaller stacks slot into the room around it. Manifexus tries many arrangements and picks the neatest one, with an even edge at the bottom.
On wide screens the dashboard uses the extra room: up to five columns of stacks instead of three, with the same easy-to-read app cards.
improved: A stack can change shape to fit (its apps in more or fewer lines, or a little wider), and it can grow slightly to close a small gap. App cards always stay full size and easy to read.
When you add, move or remove apps, fold a stack or resize the window, everything glides to its new place.
A stack name that's too long for its space shows in full when you point at it, and the rename pencil only takes room when you point at the stack, so names have more space.
fixed: A stack with 4 apps showed 3 on top and 1 alone below it, with an empty space beside it. It now fits neatly.

releases.headline: A fresh new look, easier to read everywhere.
new: Liquid Glass: the toolbar, search, New Stack and the short messages at the bottom are now Apple-style Liquid Glass. In Chrome, Brave and Edge their edges bend the light behind them; other browsers keep frosted glass.
Every screen now has the dashboard's look: Settings, Restore, Activity, app and stack details and every other sheet use the same midnight glass as your stacks.
A new font, Inter, the closest to Apple's own. It's built in, so it looks the same on Mac, Windows and Linux, even with no internet. Paths and commands use Geist Mono.
improved: Easier to read: the dashboard is drawn at full size, every text size follows Apple's type scale, nothing is smaller than 11 points, and quiet labels, links, warnings and placeholders all meet Apple's contrast guidelines.

Smoother motion everywhere: screens rise into place and their lists arrive one row after another, apps glide to their new stack, and numbers count to their new value. With Reduce Motion on, everything just appears.
Long screens fade softly under their title bar and buttons instead of being cut off.
Choices like Simple / Advanced slide to what you pick, like on iPhone.
Work in progress is easy to spot: "Moving…" and "Restarting…" shimmer while they run, a busy app has a light circling its card, and a finished job draws its check mark.
Point at a stack and a soft light follows your pointer across its glass.
Getting Started shows your progress as dots, and Manifexus welcomes you the very first time it opens.
Bigger, easier-to-hit buttons, like the rename pencil.

releases.headline: Practice on a messy server before touching yours.
new: Practice: Getting Started now lets you tidy up a pretend server that's gotten messy. Make a stack, drag apps where they belong, rename and delete stacks, then undo a change with Restore. Nothing you do there touches your server.
After practice, the tour of your real dashboard explains Restore and Settings in more depth.

releases.headline: The dashboard is back to how it was in 2.3.
improved: The dashboard looks and works as it did in version 2.3 again: the zoomed-out view with every stack at once, and dragging apps between stacks as before. Comfortable and Overview from 2.7 are gone.

releases.headline: Easy to read by default, with an Overview of everything.
new: Overview: see every stack at once, with simple app cards (icon, name and status) so the text stays easy to read. Switch with Comfortable / Overview next to Running and Stopped, or press O. Manifexus remembers which you like.
improved: The dashboard now opens at a comfortable, readable size, a little bigger when there's room, and never smaller than easy to read. Past that it scrolls.
Dragging an app when some stacks are off screen switches to Overview so every stack is in reach, then back a moment after it lands, so you see it arrive.

releases.headline: The dashboard is back to how it was in 2.3.
improved: The dashboard looks and works as it did in version 2.3 again: the zoomed-out view with every stack at once, and dragging apps between stacks as before. The size and Text Size settings and the slim header from 2.4 and 2.5 are gone.

releases.headline: A dashboard that sizes itself, and stays easy to read.
new: Text Size in Settings (Default, Large or Larger) sets the smallest the dashboard is ever drawn. Ctrl + and Ctrl − (⌘ on a Mac) change it right from the dashboard.
Scroll down to your stacks and the header becomes a slim bar at the top, with search, New Stack and every button still one click away.
improved: The dashboard sizes itself: big and comfortable with a few stacks, smaller as you add more, but never below your Text Size. With lots of stacks, app cards get simpler (icon, name and status) instead of smaller. Tap one for everything else.
Dragging an app when some stacks are off screen shows every stack as a big, readable tile to drop it on. Once you let go, the stack it went to comes into view and lights up, so you see it land.
With every stack already on screen, dragging just works in place, with no zooming.

releases.headline: Easier to read, and every stack in view when you need it.
new: Choose how big your stacks and apps are: Small, Default, Large or Larger, in Settings → Size. Ctrl + and Ctrl − (⌘ on a Mac) change it right from the dashboard.
Fit All Stacks on Screen: shrinks the dashboard to show every stack at once, but never so small it's hard to read. Past that, it scrolls.
improved: The dashboard now shows at a comfortable, readable size. When you drag an app, it zooms out to show every stack you can drop it on, lets you watch it land and the stacks settle, then zooms back in.

releases.headline: Delete an app you no longer need, safely, with everything backed up first.
new: Delete App. At the bottom of any app's Details, Delete App removes the app from your dashboard and your server, together with its own database or cache. The rest of its stack keeps running.

Everything is backed up first: its settings, its place in the stack's compose file, and its own data (its volumes and the folders only it uses). You see exactly what it keeps and how big it is before you say yes. Bring it back anytime from Restore, just as it was.
Folders it shares with other apps, like a media library or downloads, are never touched, and the screen tells you which ones those are.
fixed: Restore now puts back an app's own data even when the rest of its stack is still there.
Restoring a stack no longer restarts its other apps. Only the apps the restore brings back or changes are started; everything else keeps running.

releases.headline: Every stack shows up, and every tip is easy to read.
new: A stack whose apps aren't running right now (taken down, or never started) shows how many apps it has and a Start button that brings them all up.
improved: Point at an app card and it grows so it's easy to read, lifting above the stacks around it. Start dragging it and it shrinks back to its normal size, so it's easy to drop into another stack.
fixed: Stacks could go missing from the dashboard when none of their apps were there, for example after moving all of them away. Manifexus now finds every stack folder in your stacks location, and next to your other stacks, even though those folders aren't shared with it.

Tips that appear when you point at something were sometimes hidden behind the search field or the stacks. Every tip in the app now shows on top, stays inside the window, and has the same look (keyboard focus shows them too).

releases.headline: Everything about a stack, one tap away.
improved: Each stack now has a Details button (ⓘ), just like app cards. It opens one screen for the whole stack: its apps, Rename, Start, Restart or Stop All, Edit Compose File, where it lives, Restore and Delete. The ⋯ menus on stacks are gone.
Apps not in a stack get the same Details button, with Start, Restart or Stop All and Move into a Stack.
fixed: Menus could open hidden behind the stacks below them. Menus now always show on top.

releases.headline: Manifexus 2.0: a friendly welcome, and a tour of your dashboard.
new: Getting Started: the first time you open Manifexus, a short setup helps you choose your server's address, where new stacks go, whether to turn on Server Changes, and Simple or Advanced view.
An interactive tour shows you where everything is. It highlights each part of the dashboard and lets you try it right there: search, filter, drag an app, open Activity, Restore and more.
Run the setup and tour again anytime from Settings → Getting Started.

releases.headline: Stacks that always fit together.
improved: Stacks always fit together with no gaps between them: a layout solver tries arrangements and picks the tightest, letting a stack stack its apps in 2 or 3 lines, widen a little, or swap places when that closes a gap. Any leftover space goes at the very end. Stacks stay where they were unless moving them closes a gap.

Drag and drop moves are instant and batched: an app shows in its new stack the moment you drop it, and apps dropped into the same stack within a few seconds move together as one move behind the scenes (one change, one start). Moves between other stacks still run at the same time.
Drag an app again while it's waiting or moving: a waiting app just changes where it's going (drop it back and the move is cancelled), and a moving one goes on to its new stack once it arrives.

releases.headline: Every stack at a glance, and faster, safer drag-and-drop moves.
new: Move progress. An app that's moving shows a slim bar with how far along it is, following the real steps of the move (and saying Waiting while another move into the same stack finishes). It learns how long moves take on your server, so it gets more accurate the more you move.
improved: The dashboard now always shows every stack at once (zoomed out), so you can drag apps between stacks without scrolling. Phones keep full-size cards so they stay easy to read and tap.

Moving an app by dragging it is much faster: Manifexus backs up just that app's own data (its volumes, and its own folders in any stack folder) instead of both whole stacks. Shared folders like downloads or a media library are left alone, as a move never touches them. You can still undo every move from Restore.

Moves run side by side when they can: a move only waits for earlier moves that change one of the same stacks (where the app comes from, or where it goes). Moving A and B into one stack and C into another, C doesn't wait.
fixed: After an app finishes moving, the stacks no longer shift a second time: apps keep the same order (by name) before and after a move.
Moves no longer run at the same time. Two moves into the same stack could overwrite each other and fail ("no such service"); now each waits its turn, even from another browser tab.
Zoomed out, stacks no longer run past the right edge of the window, and they glide straight to their new places instead of overshooting.
Stacks no longer swap places when one gains or loses an app. They stay in name order, and only the stacks next to a change shift to make room.

Moving two apps into the same stack at once could fail with "no such service", or leave one out of the stack's file, because both moves rewrote that file. Moves into the same stack now take turns, and each keeps whatever changed in the stack while it waited.

releases.headline: Drag apps between stacks, see everything at once, and make a stack in one click.
new: Drag and drop. Zoom out, then drag an app onto another stack and it moves there right away. The real move runs in the background, backed up every time, and a message tells you when it's done (you can undo it from Restore). The stack glows while you drag over it. If something goes wrong, everything is put back and you're told why.
Zoom Out. See every stack at once, smaller, and drag apps between them. Tap Zoom In to go back.
New Stack in one click. A new stack appears right away with its name ready to type; press Return and it's made.
improved: Stacks and apps glide to their new places when something changes: add or move an app, or resize the window, and you can follow where everything went. An app moved to another stack flies across to it. Turned off if your device is set to reduce motion.
When the usual shapes would leave gaps (on narrower windows especially), a small stack turns, its apps stacked instead of side by side, to fill them.
A stack that sits beside taller neighbours spreads its apps evenly instead of leaving empty space at the bottom.
New stacks pop in, and an app that's restarting or moving has a soft blue ring around its card until it's done.

releases.headline: A new look: stacks in liquid glass on a deep midnight blue, and stacks that fill every gap.
improved: A stack with more apps than fit across takes the shape with no empty spots (four apps become a 2 × 2 block, three apps on a narrow window a single column), and the smaller stacks fill the space beside it. Every app card stays the same size.
Stacks are made of liquid glass: lighter, see-through panels with a bright edge that pick up a soft glow behind the dashboard. App cards are a touch brighter to match.
A deep midnight blue behind everything, so the glass has colour to catch.
An open header: the name, toolbar and search sit right on the page, lined up with your stacks. The toolbar, search and New Stack are glass capsules, with New Stack tinted blue as the main action.

releases.headline: Your stacks fit together neatly, and a stack stays until you delete it.
improved: Stacks fit together like tiles. Every app card is the same size everywhere, each stack is exactly as wide as its apps, and bigger stacks go first with smaller ones filling the space beside them, so there are no holes in the middle. When a stack gains or loses an app, or the window changes size, everything is re-fitted. A lone small stack stays small instead of stretching across the page.
Not in a Stack sits on its own at the bottom, full width, with its apps in name order (test2 before test10). It never changes how your stacks fit together.
fixed: Moving the last app out of a stack no longer makes the stack disappear. It stays on your dashboard, empty and with an icon that fits its name, until you delete it.

releases.headline: You decide when Manifexus may change your server, plus stack icons, a friendlier New Stack and Server Cleanup.
new: Server Changes. Manifexus now starts out only looking at your server (it shows your apps and can start, stop or restart them). Turn on Server Changes in Settings to let it move apps, create and delete stacks, restore backups, clean up and fix problems: it gets your server ready step by step and only switches on when everything works. Turn it off again anytime.
A friendlier New Stack. Give it any name (like Media Server) and see the folder it becomes as you type. A taken name is caught right away, and once it's made you can add apps straight from there.

Stack icons. Every stack gets its own icon from the start, guessed from its name (Downloads gets a download arrow, Media a clapperboard) in its own colour. Tap it in New Stack or Stack Details to choose any of 1,600+ symbols, 12 colours, or an app's logo. Once a stack has apps, it shows their icons, unless you picked one.
Server Cleanup. Tap Clean Up in the header to find folders no app uses anymore (empty folders, and stacks with no apps) and delete the ones you pick. Stacks are backed up first and can be restored.
improved: App cards: Move to Another Stack and Details now sit beside the app's name, and tapping a card opens its details.

A cleaner header. The version sits quietly beside Manifexus (tap it for Updates), and the light on the logo shows whether Docker is connected: point at it to see what it means and the dashboard's port, or tap it for Diagnostics.

Rename stacks and apps right on the dashboard: point at a name and tap the pencil beside it (or choose Rename in a stack's menu). Only the name you see changes, never the folder or container, and clearing it brings back the original. Names you give apps now stay after updates.
Stacks sit side by side and take only the room their apps need: a stack with one app is one column wide, so you see all your stacks at a glance instead of scrolling past empty space.
Search and New Stack are in the header, right under the toolbar, and a quiet Your Stacks line separates the header from your stacks.
Progress follows along: while a move, restore or fix runs, the screen scrolls to the step that's working (scroll up yourself and it waits for you).
Show All Steps opens every step with its commands right on top of the progress, and Back takes you straight back to it.

Each app's icon is its own: the one its page shows in the browser tab, saved in Manifexus the first time it's seen and used on every screen (cards, Details, Move, Ports, stacks). It works even when a firewall keeps Manifexus's container from reaching the app: the icon is read from the server itself.
App Details shows how long an app has really been on your server (On This Server Since), even after updates recreate it, and when it last started. The Move and Ports lists show each app's real icon.
Manifexus's own browser tab shows its icon and simply says Manifexus.
fixed: Deleting a stack removes its folder from the server, trying harder when something inside won't go, and tells you if the folder couldn't be removed instead of saying it's all gone.

releases.headline: A fresh, calmer dashboard, and problems fixed in one tap: automatically, step by step yourself, or with a private AI.
new: A fresh, calmer dashboard. Every stack is one clean panel with its apps inside, showing at a glance whether everything is running. Tap a stack's name to fold it away.
Stack actions. Each stack's ⋯ menu can Start, Restart or Stop all its apps, edit its compose file, or open the new Stack Details screen.

Apps and their databases together. A database or cache that belongs to an app (like Nextcloud's MariaDB) no longer gets its own card. The app's icon gets a small database badge, the card warns "Database stopped" if it stops, and starting the app starts it too. Its details are inside the app's Details.
Cleaner app cards. Each card shows the app's icon, name and whether it's running, with Open, Restart and Stop right there. Moving and groups are in the ⋯ menu, and tapping a card opens its details.

Open goes straight to the app's web page. Manifexus checks each port and picks the one that is really a web page (never a peer or database port). If there are several, the arrow next to Open lists them and lets you pick the default.
Real icons and names. Manifexus finds each app's icon (from the big icon sets, the app's own web page, or its GitHub project) and uses its real name, like Usenet Ultimate instead of usenet-ultimate.
Project Page. App Details links to the app's project on GitHub and shows its latest release.
Fix This. Every problem in Diagnostics' To Fix list now has three ways to fix it: Fix Automatically, Fix It Myself or Fix with AI.

Fix Automatically. For problems Manifexus knows the answer to (a settings path without its leading /, an app listed in two stacks, an app that's stopped or unhealthy) it prepares the change itself, no AI needed. You see it first, and it's backed up and saved in Restore.
Fix It Myself. Step-by-step instructions for every problem, with the exact commands to copy and buttons for the Manifexus screens that do each step. When you're done, Check Again confirms it's fixed.
Fix with AI. For everything else, a private AI built into Manifexus looks into the problem and proposes a fix. It runs on your own server: free, private, and nothing leaves your network.
improved: Running, Stopped, Stacks and Ports now live in the header. Tap Running or Stopped to show only those apps, or Ports to see which app uses each port.
Stacks and Groups are now two big titles you tap between, with search beside them and one + button for New Stack and New Group.

Fixing has its own screen. It shows the problem, works on it step by step, then shows the change with a before and after of every file: Make Changes, Do It Myself or Not Now. After the change it runs the checks again to confirm the problem is gone. One problem, start to finish.
The AI knows what Manifexus can do: when a screen does the job (Move, Restore, Settings…) it offers a button that opens it, instead of terminal steps.

The AI chooses the model for each problem by its real speed on your server: when the smarter model is about as fast, it does everything. Thinking is kept short on slow processors unless the problem needs it.
If the AI can't come up with a change that checks out, it stops and explains instead of trying again and again, and it no longer repeats the same lookup.

Smarter AI recommendations for every server. Setup measures your server's memory speed in a second or two, combines it with its processor, graphics card and free memory, and recommends the smartest model that works in a reasonable time there, with the reason and the expected time. Usually that's one model: a second is only suggested when it would be clearly faster.

Estimates that learn your server. Every fix measures how fast the model really reads and writes on your server, and corrects the estimates for the other models too, so recommendations and progress times get more accurate the more you use it.
Progress while the AI works counts the whole step (loading, reading and writing), not just reading, so the time left is much closer to reality.
Removing every AI model starts setup again from the beginning, with fresh recommendations.

The AI reads much less before starting, so fixes are faster: logs are boiled down to errors, warnings and the latest lines with repeats merged (a noisy 31,000-character log becomes a few lines), settings files show only the lines around the setting in question, Diagnostics only shows problems, and its own instructions are shorter. The fix for a broken setting now reads about 40% less.
Each AI step shows what it read: its instructions, the problem, and what it looked up.

A guided setup for the built-in AI. The first time you choose Fix with AI, a few short steps walk you through it: pick the AI models (picked for your server), what it may do, what it may look at, and how hard it thinks. The download starts as soon as you pick the models and keeps going while you choose the rest. Change any of it later in Settings → Built-in AI.
Choose what the AI may look at. App logs, files on your server, Activity and Restore, and server details can each be turned off. Passwords, tokens and keys are always hidden from it.

The recommended models download as one pipeline with one progress view: disk space is checked for all of them first, they download one after another (smallest first), and each is checked, loaded into memory and tested while the next one downloads, so everything is ready sooner.

Every step of getting a model ready is shown as it happens, with download speed, time left, which part it's on, loading into memory, and a test that measures how fast it is on your server. Then it starts on your problem as soon as it's ready.
While the AI works, you see each step as it happens: what it looked up, which model is reading and how much, a progress bar with the time left, and how long every step took.

Much faster fixes. Manifexus looks up the obvious things (the file or app in question) before the AI starts, and small file changes are written as a one-line edit instead of the whole file, so a fix like a wrong setting takes one AI round instead of several.

Choose Automatically (in Settings → Built-in AI, on by default). Each problem gets the right model and amount of thinking: simple ones stay quick, tricky ones go to the fixer and think it through, and if the quick helper gets stuck the fixer takes over. The fixer only runs when there's enough free memory at that moment.
The AI's explanations appear all at once when they're ready, nicely formatted: numbered steps, code blocks with a Copy button, tables and highlighted names and paths.
Activity has new Fixes and Fix with AI filters.
fixed: When a fix finishes, a Done button is always there to close it.
No more garbled patches behind a screen while the AI starts up.
Undo Fix no longer says it failed when it actually put the file back.
Fix with AI no longer fails with "fetch failed" after 5 minutes when it takes a long time on a slow processor. If the AI engine really stops responding, you get a plain explanation.
Fix with AI waits until setup is completely finished (every model downloaded, tested and loaded into memory), so the right model can be chosen and nothing else slows it down.
The progress line no longer claims the AI has finished reading when it hasn't. Past the time estimate, it says so and keeps a moving bar.
The AI's look at recent Activity shows the real error messages instead of "[object Object]".
Removing an AI model no longer shows "Unexpected end of JSON input" when it actually worked, and tapping Remove on a model that's already gone isn't an error.
AI fixes no longer stay "In progress" in Activity forever. Each ends as done, failed (with the reason) or stopped.

releases.headline: Meet Ask Manifexus: a private AI, built in, that can look into problems and fix them with your OK.
new: Ask Manifexus. Tap Ask in the header and ask anything about your apps: why something stopped, what changed, what's using the most memory.
It runs on your own server. It's free and private, and nothing leaves your network.
Picked for your server. Manifexus checks your memory, processor and graphics card, and recommends AI models that fit without slowing your apps down.
Downloads that don't give up. If the connection drops, the AI download picks up where it stopped, even after a restart. Every download is checked before it's used.
Fix with AI. One tap from the To Fix list in Diagnostics, and it works out what's wrong.
You're always in control. Every change is shown to you first, with a before and after of every file. It's backed up, and you can undo it from Restore.
Choose how much it may do on its own: Look Only, Ask Before Changes, Fix Routine Things or Expert.
Learn how it's done. Turn on Show Commands (or choose Advanced in Settings) to see the command behind every step, with a plain explanation of each part.
Do It Myself. Every AI fix can be done by hand instead, one step at a time, with the terminal a tap away.
Activity → Commands. A learning log of every command behind your recent changes, and How It Was Done on every activity.
improved: Updates now show version numbers and notes like these, instead of build codes.
Activity has a new Fixes filter.
fixed: On phones, the dashboard no longer shifts sideways by a few pixels.
If an AI model can't download, you get a clear reason and a Try Again button.
Updating Manifexus keeps your settings, history, backups and AI models, even if no data folder was set up. Diagnostics now tells you if one is missing.

releases.headline: The first full release: move, restore and understand your Docker apps, all in one place.
new: Restore. Go back to before any move or delete. Every change keeps a backup, and restores can be undone too.
Activity. A complete record of everything Manifexus does, with the exact reason when something fails.
Diagnostics. Health checks in plain words, with a To Fix list that stays until each issue is fixed.
App Details. Every app's health, resources, storage, network and what it has printed, in one place.
Software updates that restore the previous version automatically if the new one doesn't start.
improved: One clean, consistent design throughout, with every screen the same size.
Settings save as you change them.
fixed: A leftover app entry in one stack can no longer break moving apps into it.
